discussion_comments.comment_body: `readPersistedChatMessages` returns `[]` for a messages file with an empty or missing `messages` array, so this is true for that case too. `handleSessionResume` then answers `session_messages_not_found` for an empty history, and since that isn't `unsupported_command` the start fails, where before it went through `session.create` with `[]`. Should this be `initialMessages.length > 0`, like the `callerInitialMessages` check above?

I fixed this in 54ee82110. Clearing a custom base URL now sends an explicit `baseUrl: null` reset through the live connection contract. Core rebuilds provider configuration after removing the stale custom URL, so LM Studio returns to its manifest default while an empty string remains a distinct literal value. Regression coverage exercises the custom-to-default transition and transport parsing.

after `ensureSessionPersisted`, if `artifacts` is still missing the block falls through into `startResolvedSession` and can still replace the live entry. `ensureSessionPersisted` normally assigns artifacts or throws, so this is the rare null-return case, but that is exactly the orphaning path this PR is closing. would throwing here be safer than falling through?

Fixed in ebd35d381: the catch is gone. workingSubproject now returns empty only for a directory git says is not its own repository root (an uninitialized submodule), and undefined when the path isn't a directory; in that case the diff falls through to the normal reader path, so the reader's binary (content: null) and truncated flags are kept and real read errors propagate. A missing path is still handled by the reader itself, which already returns empty for deletions. Test covers a submodule replaced by a file with truncated: true.

In general, it is better if we can reflect the "only set for `beforeRun`" in a TypeScript shape which has `{foo: "beforeRun", entry: "run" | "continue", ...}` so the rest of the system can use these fields in a typesafe way. Also possible to lift a property out of an object by construction to relate these fields with some other state. (Does that make sense? TL;DR, can we use the type system here to communicate "only set for `beforeRun`" and benefit from checking?)

Valid, fixed in the latest push. A Retry click carries no attachments of its own: protobuf decodes the omitted `images` field as `[]`, so `images ?? retry.images` kept the empty list. The retry now uses `images?.length ? images : retry.images`, so the failed start's attachments go to the retried sandbox unless the response actually carries some. Covered by `keeps the original attachments when Retry arrives with the webview's empty image list` in `SdkController.test.ts`, which sends Retry with `[]` and fails without the fix.

The same push merges `main` into this branch (the only conflict was in `state-keys.ts`, where `main` removed the focus-chain setting next to the new cloud keys). On the merged result, the full extension type check, vitest (1,452), `test:cloud` (23), the bun unit tests and the webview tests (584) all pass.

We probably almost always call this, so we could simplify the whole thing by always initializing `turnAccepted` in the constructor, make that type non-null and avoid some ?s, and avoid the conditional in `whenTurnAccepted`.

Stylistically, think `turnAccepted.then(...)` or `await turnAccepted` read better than `whenTurnAccepted().then(...)` or `await whenTurnAccepted`, so consider renaming `whenTurnAccepted`.

Half right, and the fix is the other half. The `null` is deliberate: an explicit `undefined` is swallowed by the parameter default, so the unlisted-model case would silently get the effort options instead of none. The bug was that my edit to widen the signature to `| null` did not apply, leaving the annotation saying `| undefined` while the body already normalised `null`. Signature corrected rather than the call site.
